problem:
Find the curvature at an arbitrary point on the curve $r(t)$ given that its derivative ${r}^{′}(t)$ and the derivative of the corresponding unit tangent ${T}^{′}(t)$ are as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t)=⟨\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩,\,{T}^{′}(t)=⟨\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
Find the curvature at an arbitrary point on the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by its arc length $s$, where

$$
r(s)=⟨\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{2}s),\,-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{2}s),\,-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{2}s)⟩,\,0\le s<\sqrt{2}\pi .
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
Let $T(s)$ denote the unit tangent to the given curve as a function of the arc length $s.$ Since we are given the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by the arc length $s$, we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
κ(s)=‖{T}^{′}(s)‖=‖{r}^{″}(s)‖
$$

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(s)$ and ${r}^{″}(s)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(s) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{2}s)),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{2}s)),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{2}s))⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{2}s)\cdot \sqrt{2},\,-\frac{1}{2}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{2}s))\cdot \sqrt{2},\,-\frac{1}{2}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{2}s))\cdot \sqrt{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{2}s),\,\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{2}s),\,\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{2}s)⟩ \\ {r}^{″}(s) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{2}s)),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{2}s)),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{2}s))⟩ \\  & =⟨(-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{2}s))\cdot \sqrt{2},\,\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{2}s)\cdot \sqrt{2},\,\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{2}s)\cdot \sqrt{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨-\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{2}s),\,\operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{2}s),\,\operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{2}s)⟩\end{aligned}
$$

   

Finally, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(s) & =‖{r}^{″}(s)‖ \\  & =\sqrt{{(-\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡\sqrt{2}s)}^{2}+{(\operatorname{cos}⁡\sqrt{2}s)}^{2}+{(\operatorname{cos}⁡\sqrt{2}s)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{2{sin}^{2}⁡(\sqrt{2}s)+2{cos}^{2}⁡(\sqrt{2}s)} \\  & =\sqrt{2({sin}^{2}⁡(\sqrt{2}s)+{cos}^{2}⁡(\sqrt{2}s))} \\  & =\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
